checklist_item: Identify the study as developing or evaluating a multivariable prediction model, the target population, and the outcome.
Report the study according to the TRIPOD+AI for Abstracts checklist.
Explain the healthcare context and rationale, including existing prediction models.
Describe the target population, intended purpose, care pathway, and intended users.
Describe known health inequalities between sociodemographic groups.
Specify the objectives and whether the study develops or evaluates a prediction model.
Describe data sources, rationale, and representativeness separately for development and evaluation data.
Specify the start and end dates of participant accrual and follow-up.
Describe the study setting, including number and location of centers.
Describe participant eligibility criteria.
Describe treatments received and how they were handled, if relevant.
Describe data preprocessing and quality checking, including consistency across sociodemographic groups.
Define the outcome and time horizon, how and when it was assessed, its rationale, and consistency across groups.
For subjective outcomes, describe outcome assessor qualifications and demographic characteristics.
Report actions used to blind outcome assessment.
Describe the choice and any preselection of initial predictors.
Define predictors, how and when they were measured, and any blinding.
For subjectively interpreted predictors, describe assessor qualifications and demographic characteristics.
Explain how study size was determined and justify its sufficiency, including any calculation.
Describe how missing data were handled and reasons for omitting data.
Describe how data were used for model development and evaluation, including partitioning.
Describe predictor handling, including transformations and standardization.
Specify model types, rationale, model-building steps, tuning, and internal validation.
Describe handling and quantification of heterogeneity across clusters.
Specify performance measures and plots, their rationale, and model comparisons.
Describe model updating arising from evaluation.
Describe how predictions were calculated during model evaluation.
Describe class-imbalance methods and any subsequent recalibration.
Describe approaches used to address model fairness and their rationale.
Specify model output and any classification thresholds and how they were identified.
Identify differences between development and evaluation data.
Name the ethics committee and describe consent or waiver.
Report funding sources and funder roles.
Declare conflicts of interest and financial disclosures.
State where the protocol can be accessed or that no protocol was prepared.
Provide study registration or state that the study was not registered.
Describe availability of study data.
Describe availability of analytical code.
Describe patient and public involvement or state that there was none.
Describe participant flow, outcome counts, and follow-up time; consider a diagram.
Report participant characteristics, dates, predictors, treatments, events, follow-up, missingness, and demographic differences.
For model evaluation, compare distributions of important predictors and outcomes with development data.
Report participant and event counts for each analysis.
Provide the full prediction model or accessible code/object/API and restrictions.
Report performance estimates with confidence intervals and key subgroup results.
Report heterogeneity in performance across clusters, if examined.
Report any model updating and subsequent performance.
Interpret main results, including fairness, in relation to objectives and previous studies.
Discuss limitations and effects on bias, uncertainty, and generalizability.
Describe how poor-quality or unavailable input data should be handled during implementation.
Describe required user interaction and expertise.
Discuss next research steps for applicability and generalizability.
